reply.subject: RM_LivingBolt

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one shared scale on a checkerboard. South and east both show a faceted, rust-and-steel nut lying on its side, with its threaded bore facing left, a short threaded shaft, and a hex bolthead to the right. There is a dark crack across the nut. North shows the same assembly tipped diagonally: the bolthead at upper left (it has a crack too), the shaft in the middle, and the nut at lower right with its bore facing right. The colour is dull gunmetal with orange rust rims. The outline is clean and dark, and there is no shadow.
observed.south.png: A full-resolution south view. A cracked, faceted nut lies on its side with its bore open to the viewer at left, joined by a threaded shank to a hex bolthead at right. The metal is dulled and rusted, the shading is painterly, and the cut-out is clean.
observed.east.png: Nearly the same composition as south: the nut on the left with its bore showing, a crack running diagonally across the nut, then the threaded shank and the hex bolthead on the right. It is slightly shorter than south. It is painterly and rusted, with a clean cut-out.
observed.north.png: The assembly is tipped about 45 degrees: the bolthead is up and to the left, the threads run diagonally, and the nut is down and to the right with its bore visible at the right side. It reads as the same object lying at a different angle. It is painterly with a clean cut-out.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the candidate is a tiny brown speck beside the vanilla human, a small fraction of a cell. In the normal-play inset it is practically invisible next to the human and the rat.
observed.living_reference.png: The living art: an upright, polished chrome assembly, with a faceted bolthead on top, a short collar or shaft, and a faceted octagonal nut below with a bore through it. The bore faces the camera on south, shows at the side on east, and the nut is plain on north. Bright chrome with orange-rimmed reflections.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: A limbless machine corpse lying on its side. South shows the nut's bore end toward the camera, which is the object's front. A corpse lying down makes front/rear facing a matter of pose.

NORTH_REAR.seen: There is no face or eyes on any facing. North shows the assembly tipped diagonally, and the visible bore is a machined hole, not a face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three are drawn at the angled game camera with side facets visible. None is a plan view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The 46% height spread comes from pose: north is tilted diagonally, so it is taller and narrower. The nut and bolthead are about the same pixel size in all three views.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The same nut, shank, bolthead, rust palette and crack appear on every facing. The parts stay in a consistent arrangement as the object turns.

SIGNATURE.seen: The chrome nut with a bolthead is clearly legible, and the corpse cues (tipped over, cracked, rusted and dulled) are present.

ALIEN.seen: A mechanoid machine, not an Earth animal. Its geometry is faceted rather than a plain hex nut.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1) No limbs and no face: a machined nut with a bolthead. Present. 2) Corpse lying tipped on its side, cracked and dulled: present on all three, with a crack on the nut on south and east and on the bolthead on north.

CANON.seen: The card lists no canon Must show lines.

STYLE.seen: Painterly metal rendering with a clean dark outline. Not cel-shaded, not cute, not a photo.

OURS.seen: Derived from the mod's own living art: the same faceted nut and bolthead design, rusted. Not donor art.

ALPHA.seen: Clean transparent background with no ground patch or shadow under any facing.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: It is still a large nut with a bolthead and keeps the faceted, advanced geometry. The shine is deliberately dulled because the card's corpse brief asks for 'dulled, rusted'. It is drawn at 0.1 cells.

SCALE.seen: A button-sized speck beside the human, matching drawSize 0.1.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell the 0.1-cell corpse is about 3 px and invisible. This is inherent to the specified size; advisory only.

findings.seen: The corpse is about 3 px and not distinguishable from the ground at 32 px per cell.
findings.quote: At 32 px per cell does it read as a few bold shapes apart from the ground?
findings.fix: Keep the drawSize the owner specified, and keep the silhouette high-contrast with a dark outline so the speck reads as metal against soil.

reply.subject: RM_LivingBolt
reply.image_seen: Image 1 compares three metal nut-and-bolt corpses; images 2–3 show horizontal cracked specimens with different nut perspectives; image 4 shows a diagonally tipped specimen; image 5 shows button-sized game scale; image 6 shows the upright, shinier living reference.

concerns.evidence: South and east share the horizontal resting pose but show distinct viewing angles: south exposes a broad threaded bore, while east shows a narrower bore on the left edge and a broader solid side facet. The nut facets, crack placement and bolthead perspective differ visibly; these are distinct views of the same mechanism.

The corpses retain silver chrome facets, dark metal recesses and orange edge accents matching the living reference. Their tarnished surfaces and visible nut cracks implement the explicit corpse requirement, 'tipped onto its side, dulled, rusted, a crack in the nut.' Remaining bright highlights preserve the underlying chrome identity.
